text:
Sam (Support): FYI customer ACME reporting intermittent 502/504s from the /v1/rerank endpoint during a traffic burst this morning. p95 jumped ~80ms -> ~1.8s, lots of gateway timeouts and client retries. Can SRE/Runtime triage?

Rita (SRE): ACK. Do we have request IDs or example traces? Which model and batch size were they using? Any rate/throughput numbers?

Sam (Support): Provided a transcript and request IDs to the customer, forwarding here: request_id=01G7X2Y8A9, request_id=01G7X2Y9B0. They hit ~650 qps for ~3m, batch_size=20, concurrency reported ~30 per client. Model used: "redwood/rerank-v1". Sample payload I asked them to repro with:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/rerank 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"query":"best laptop","documents":[{"id":"1","text":"..."}, ...]}'
```

Kevin (Eng Runtime): Thanks — this smells like backend worker pool saturation + gateway queue timeouts. Gateway returns 502/504 when backend doesn't respond before proxy timeout, and client retries amplify the load. Two immediate asks: (1) grab gateway logs around those request_ids to confirm 502 origin, (2) check rerank backend pod metrics: queue length, threadpool wait, and CPU/GPU saturation.

Rita (SRE): I pulled gateway logs for 01G7X2Y8A9: gateway -> upstream=rerrank-proxy returned 502 after 5.0s. Backend didn't log completion. Looking at metrics, rerank-worker pool had a backlog of ~140 requests; p95 for service went to ~2.1s. Autoscale didn't react quickly — policy min=3 pods, max=6, we were at 3.

Infra-oncall: Autoscaler was rate-limited by cluster quota in the region due to another team's burst; we hit a soft limit so it capped at 3. Manually bumped the nodepool + scaled deployment to 5 while we investigate.

Kevin (Eng Runtime): Good catch. Two mitigation options for support/customer: (A) reduce requested batch_size to 8-10 to lower per-request work; (B) add client-side retry/backoff and increase request timeout to 10s temporarily so gateway doesn't prematurely 502 and amplify retries. We should also enable a fallback model variant with lower CPU work if available.

Sam (Support): Shared those workarounds with ACME. They asked for a reproducible loadtest to prove it. Kevin, can you provide a simple repro command we can give them?

Kevin (Eng Runtime): Yep — here's a simple vegeta and curl example to simulate their pattern:
```
# payload.json contains one query + 20 docs
vegeta attack -duration=180s -rate=700 -connections=200 -body=payload.json 'POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/rerank' | vegeta report
# or a quick hey run to reproduce concurrency spikes
hey -n 10000 -c 60 -m POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/rerank
```
Note: set batch docs to 20 and concurrency around 30-60 to match their load. We recommend starting at lower rate and ramping.

Dinesh (Support): Heads-up: customer is worried about billing impact from retries. We credited them for the extra calls while we triage. Billing team notified.

Rita (SRE): Action items: (1) Keven/Eng to add a short-term rate-limit at gateway per-customer to prevent retry storms (2) Runtime team to add a health-check metric that will short-circuit large batches when queue depth > threshold (3) Infra to review autoscaler quota so it can scale when rerank spikes.

Kevin (Eng Runtime): I'll open an internal ticket for a gateway per-tenant concurrency cap and add a quick patch to recommend reducing max batch size in SDK for this model. Also will push a small telemetry change to emit queue_depth on the /metrics endpoint.

Infra-oncall: Nodepool scaled and we observed error rate drop after ~90s. p95 came back down to ~120ms. Leaving manual scale while we get quota fixed.

Sam (Support): Customer confirmed reduced errors after we suggested batch_size=8 + SDK backoff. They still want a root cause writeup and steps to avoid in future.

Rita (SRE): I'll draft an incident note linking logs, request_ids, autoscaler events, and mitigation steps. Assigning to Kevin for runtime follow-ups.

LoadTest-bot: Deployment: loadtest-tooling v0.9.1 promoted to staging at 2024-06-12T15:23:10Z.

Sam (Support): Thanks everyone. Summarized reply sent to ACME with repro commands, short-term mitigations, and ETA for internal fixes. Will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
